findings.summary: Stale comments misattribute the cross-generation permit to the materializer. dd_replay.py:238-241 states 'The generation-aware permit of an older generation's inherited chain is the materializer's job (dd_materializer), which reads the committed entries at the seal', and the regression docstring at tests/test_dd_replay.py:794-796 repeats it. In this change the materializer guard is deliberately flat and explicitly disclaims the permit (dd_materializer.py:284-292); the permit is delivered by configure's index scoping (dd/feedback_scope.py). Behaviour is unaffected -- the replayer's fail-closed refusal is exactly what routes the restart to a real configure that scopes -- but the comments describe the attempt-5 design and point a future maintainer at the wrong component.

Product consistency between d57ab2279de89559c9a0350bbb51c0391900af14 and 3b97fa471b2aaa58c041e3589478ec0e6f9e8076 was not verified mechanically: this reviewer has read-only file inspection and no shell or Git execution, so the required `git diff --exit-code ... ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not run. The worktree's .git/refs/heads/main reads 3b97fa471b2aaa58c041e3589478ec0e6f9e8076, so the files inspected are the subject commit's, and the only attempt-6 additions visible under .dev-dispatch/ are the rc-6ab2d9b3 review artifact and the feedback index -- consistent with a metadata-only materialization, but not an establishment of it. This is not a qualification of the APPROVE.

The sealed implement handoff records `work_head_commit` 6a06afacd4f25603d86d8e9bbcf5f7320bd511fd, while the dispatch context names d57ab2279de89559c9a0350bbb51c0391900af14 as the product commit (`work_head_commit`). This matches the metadata-only-seal pattern every prior attempt in this development shows and was noted by the attempt-3, -4 and -5 final reviews, but the two identities are not interchangeable. Recorded for the record; not a qualification of the APPROVE.
